<reflection>
The second experiment with higher catalyst concentration (0.05 M) successfully increased differentiation among mechanisms, as evidenced by the wider spread in negative log-likelihood values compared to the first experiment. M3 now has the lowest NLL, but several other mechanisms (M5, M9, M20, M10) are within ~1 unit, indicating they still have non-negligible support. The aim to stress differences by varying catalyst concentration was achieved, but further discrimination is needed.
</reflection>
<hypothesis>
To reduce uncertainty across the entire set of mechanisms, I propose introducing initial product to test for product-related effects. Many mechanisms involve product inhibition or product-dependent deactivation (e.g., M12: P+cat deactivation, M17: P+catS deactivation), while reversible mechanisms (M1, M2, etc.) may show backward reaction influence. By comparing with run 1 (identical S and cat but no product), we can isolate the impact of product on kinetics. This condition (S=1.0 M, cat=0.01 M, P=0.1 M) is moderate and avoids saturation, while probing a new dimension that discriminates multiple mechanisms simultaneously, including deactivation pathways and reversibility.
</hypothesis>
